title: 14.7 NeuroPilot: A 28nm, 69.4fJ/node and 0.22ns/node, 32×32 Mimetic-Path-Searching CIM-Macro with Dynamic-Logic Pilot PE and Dual-Direction Searching
problem: Path-finding algorithms for autonomous micro-robots, VLSI routing, and wavefront propagation traditionally use digital accelerators; existing mimetic-CIM solutions suffer from inefficient single-direction searching (underutilization), poor DFF-based storage (power/area/leakage), and limited processing windows for large maps.
motivation: Autonomous navigation and path planning are critical for mobile robotics and electronic design; CIM architectures offer superior power-area-delay vs. digital approaches by integrating SRAM within processing elements.
method: NeuroPilot implements dual-direction searching (DDS) to accelerate by utilizing full search time, uses a dynamic-logic pilot PE with outspread pre-charge (OPC) circuit for superior PPA and reduced leakage vs. DFF storage, and enables 3-step coarse/fine-path (TsCFP) flow for efficient large-map navigation.
key_novelty: Dual-direction searching with dynamic-logic pilot PE and automated coarse/fine-path flow for efficient large-scale path-finding in CIM architecture.
contributions: Dual-direction searching (DDS) doubling search efficiency vs. single-direction approaches
Dynamic-logic pilot PE with outspread pre-charge (OPC) for superior PPA and minimal leakage
3-step coarse/fine-path (TsCFP) flow enabling large-map navigation without task failure
Achieves 3670M nodes/s search rate, 213.6µm² PE area, 69.4fJ/node energy, 0.22ns/node latency
limitations: Comparison with state-of-the-art digital pathfinding and multi-macro CIM systems not discussed.
primary_theme: 28nm CIM path-finding processor with dual-direction search and dynamic-logic PEs
